unlisted_practices: Legislators should conduct a regulatory impact assessment of new regulation after clearly defining its intended purpose.
Legislators should subject new regulation to conformity assessment against performance requirements by an independent oversight body.
Regulators should monitor the real-world performance of regulation after implementation through post-market surveillance-style ex-post analysis.
Regulators should perform root cause analysis and corrective and preventive actions when incidents occur in the implementation of regulation.
Regulators should phase in new regulatory requirements by device type and notified body responsibility, and make IT systems optional until they are complete.
The EU should address gaps in AI-enabled medical device regulation through flexible guidance or common specifications under the MDR rather than new legislation.
The EU should pilot a dedicated expert panel for AI-enabled medical devices and digital health technologies to provide regulatory science expertise.
Regulators should prioritize small and medium-sized enterprises in regulatory sandbox and pilot programs.

Manufacturers should develop all digital health technologies close to medical device state of the art, using a quality management system and good machine learning practice, even when enforcement discretion applies.
Regulators should adopt predetermined change control plans for managing changes to AI-enabled software, supported by robust post-market surveillance and real-world evidence.
Regulators should integrate regulatory approval with health technology assessment for AI-enabled medical devices.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint/commentary discussing regulatory frameworks and governance approaches for AI and digital health technologies across the EU, US, and UK.
